plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 14: Conjugated Compounds and Ultraviolet Spectroscopy
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-trace ultraviolet absorption spectrum of 1,3-butadiene plotted over a pink gradient field. The vertical axis is labeled "Absorbance", carries a magenta arrow pointing up beside the label, and runs from 0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks every 0.2. The horizontal axis reads "Wavelength (nm)", is followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, and spans 200 to 400 with labeled ticks every 20 nm. One magenta curve enters at the left edge near 0.34, climbs steeply to a rounded maximum just under 0.9 at about 215 nm, then falls sharply through 240 nm to roughly 0.07, after which it declines almost imperceptibly along a near-horizontal tail to about 0.03 at the right edge. A short annotation just above and right of the crest reads "lambda max = 217 nm". With the zero baseline at the bottom of the chart rather than the top, absorption registers as a peak rising off a flat floor, and the eye is meant to fix on that lone crest against the featureless tail beyond 250 nm. The trace records the wavelength of strongest absorption for a simple conjugated diene, the reading from which molar absorptivity is calculated.

interactionPlan.concept: A UV absorption spectrum records how strongly a conjugated molecule absorbs light at each wavelength, and lambda max is the wavelength at which that absorbance reaches its highest value.

interactions.label: Wavelength (nm)
interactions.teaches: Absorbance varies continuously with wavelength, and λmax is simply the wavelength where the curve reaches its highest point — scrubbing reveals the crest near 217 nm and the near-zero tail beyond 250 nm

interactions.label: Region focus
interactions.teaches: The diagnostically useful absorption of 1,3-butadiene is concentrated at the short-wavelength crest; the long-wavelength tail carries almost no absorbance and is not used for identifying the conjugated system

demo_steps.title: The full spectrum
demo_steps.narration: The magenta curve shows how strongly 1,3-butadiene absorbs UV light at each wavelength from 200 to 400 nm. One prominent peak stands out against a nearly flat tail.

demo_steps.title: Finding λmax
demo_steps.narration: Drag the wavelength slider — the dot rides the curve and the readout updates. At 217 nm absorbance is highest (~0.87); this crest is λmax, the value used to characterize the conjugated system.

demo_steps.title: The featureless tail
demo_steps.narration: Beyond about 250 nm the molecule barely absorbs. Scrubbing through the tail shows absorbance near zero — all the diagnostic information lives at the short-wavelength peak.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: λmax is not a special marker placed on the spectrum — it is simply the wavelength at the top of the absorption peak, and for 1,3-butadiene essentially all UV absorption is concentrated at that single crest near 217 nm.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Render as a clean 2D line chart over a subtle vertical pink-to-white gradient background. Magenta curve with the exact shape described: steep rise from ~0.34 at 200 nm to a rounded maximum just under 0.9 near 217 nm, sharp descent through 240 nm, then a long near-flat tail to ~0.03 at 400 nm. Axis labels in bold with magenta directional arrows (up for Absorbance, right for Wavelength). The 'λmax = 217 nm' annotation sits just above-right of the crest. Slider drives a small filled dot constrained to the curve plus a numeric readout (wavelength and absorbance). Toggle highlights: 'Peak' dims everything except a band around 210–225 nm with the crest emphasized; 'Tail' dims everything left of 250 nm and shades the tail region; 'Full spectrum' shows no highlighting.

authoredContext:
Note that UV spectra differ from IR spectra in how they are presented. For historical reasons, IR spectra are usually displayed so that the baseline corresponding to zero absorption runs across the top of the chart and a valley indicates an absorption, whereas UV spectra are displayed with the baseline at the bottom of the chart so that a peak indicates an absorption (the figure).

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene, λmax = 217 nm.

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene shows a peak at (217, 0.85) where lambda max equals 217 nanometers. The x-axis and y-axis represent wavelength and absorbance, respectively.
